correctness.rationale: The full cyclic Weyl coefficient basis and the character diagonalization reconstruct projector Gram rank as exactly the nonzero self-ambiguity count. Every lag overlap has at most two explicit intervals. One interval has \(\gcd(N,\ell)-1\) nontrivial zeros; two intervals factor exactly as \((1-z^k)(1+z^a)/(1-z)\), and the root sets intersect in \(\beta_d(a)\) by a solvable modular congruence, giving an exact per-lag formula with all b=0 exceptions treated separately. Odd-dimensional informational completeness reduces to an interval of integers avoiding the least prime divisor; even-dimensional failure comes from the half-period lag. For dimensions \(2^q\) each order-\(2^j\) frequency has a sharp lower bound \(N/2^j\) zero lags, with equality for odd lengths above half, and exact excess for divisible lengths. A supplied exact integer polynomial/cyclotomic checker, executed from the current candidate package path, confirms every lag and length for \(3\le N\le24\); no finite check is substituted for the all-N proof.

value.rationale: The work answers the naturally parameterized quantitative rank problem for a canonical deterministic window family. It identifies all observable matrix directions and all arithmetic rank losses, not just existence of a frame or a sufficient phase-retrieval assumption. Its sharp odd parity/least-prime-divisor threshold and exact power-of-two maximal rank \(N^2-(N/2)\log_2 N\) with all optimizing rectangular lengths guide linear Gabor tomography design. The \(N=8,9\) rank profiles show counterintuitive nonmonotonicity as a rectangular window grows. This precise rank information is not a simple restatement of the general ambiguity criterion or of earlier sufficient recovery assertions, and the proof involves two-arc Fourier cancellations and character-order accounting.
